svg.title: Order management system: database section cheat sheet
svg.text: Polyglot persistence: one store per access pattern, Postgres is the source of truth
1. PostgreSQL: source of truth for orders, payments, inventory
written in the same txn as the order
What to say in the interview
1. ACID, source of truth for orders, payments, inventory; strong consistency
2. Normalized schema + FKs; index the access paths: (user_id, created_at DESC)
3. Concurrency: MVCC, row lock (SELECT FOR UPDATE) or optimistic version on stock
4. Idempotency key UNIQUE on payments: safe retries, no double charge
5. Transactional outbox + CDC (Debezium) → Kafka → Cassandra, ES, ClickHouse
6. Scale reads: replicas (async lag), PgBouncer; partition orders by month
7. Scale writes: shard by user_id (Citus or app-level) only when one primary is not enough
2. Redis: cart, session, stock counters, cache
Lua example: reserve stock atomically (EVALSHA with KEYS = stock:{sku_id}, ARGV = qty)
else return -1 end -- out of stock, no oversell
What to say in the interview
3. Cluster mode: 16,384 hash slots; replicas per shard for failover
4. Eviction policy: LRU / LFU / FIFO / TTL
5. Cache stampede: request coalescing, cache warm-up
6. Cache consistency: invalidation, short TTL, eventual consistency
7. Hot keys: replicate hot keys, application (local) cache, rate limiter
8. Lua scripts (EVAL / EVALSHA): atomic multi-step logic in one round trip; keep short, same-slot keys
3. Cassandra: order history at scale (write-heavy, query-first)
How data is stored: one table per query
PRIMARY KEY ((user_id, month_bucket), created_at DESC, order_id)
Partition (u_42, 2026-10): rows sorted on disk by created_at DESC
Partition (order 9f1): events stored in time order
What to say in the interview
1. High write throughput: LSM tree (commit log → memtable → SSTable)
2. Predictable access pattern: one table per query
3. Consistent hashing ring + virtual nodes; gossip protocol
4. Tunable consistency: R + W > N; RF = 3, LOCAL_QUORUM
5. Wide-column database; Bloom filter per SSTable skips disk reads
6. Tombstones + compaction strategies; time-bucket keys avoid unbounded partitions
7. PK = user_id (+ bucket), clustering = created_at DESC; no joins / ad-hoc queries
What to say in the interview
1. Full-text search, fuzzy search; filtering, ranking, aggregations; auto-complete
2. Text analysis → inverted index creation → BM25 relevance scoring
3. Derived from Postgres via CDC: eventually consistent, rebuildable
PARTITION BY month; ORDER BY (order_date, category_id)
What to say in the interview
1. Columnar OLAP: reads only needed columns, high compression, fast aggregations
2. Append-only batch inserts from Kafka; not for OLTP, no frequent row updates
3. Use for: revenue by day/category, funnels, dashboards over billions of rows
Data flow: how the stores stay in sync
Redis in front of reads: cache-aside, cart, session, stock counters, idempotency
